sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: signaling habits, turn technique, one-way turns, lanes and crossovers, passing limits, trucks, backing, parking rules, emergency parking, handicap spaces and angle parking
Confusable pairs and continuation facts; each block ties to one manual page, and any hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec09-R01 | anchor: A01
Signal every time you change direction, even when no one seems to be around, because the car you do not see is the most dangerous. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec09-R02 | anchor: A01
When leaving a curb, signal long enough for oncoming traffic to know you are pulling out of the parked position. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec09-R03 | anchor: A01
Move into the correct turn lane as early as possible, sooner on faster roads, choose your gear before the intersection and accelerate slightly through the turn. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec09-R04 | anchor: A01
Do not enter an intersection to turn if traffic ahead could keep you from finishing the turn before the light changes; wait behind the stop line. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec09-R05 | anchor: A02
In a left turn, keep the wheels straight until you reach the turn point, just before the imaginary center of the intersection. [A02]
Why it matters: group left turns; confusable when to start turning the wheel.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec09-R06 | anchor: A02
Where a lane is marked for left turns, turn only from that lane, and in multiple turn lanes stay in your starting lane all the way through. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec09-R07 | anchor: A02
Turning left from one one-way street onto another, you may go on red after a full stop unless a No Turn on Red sign is posted. [A02]
Why it matters: group turns on red; confusable one-way onto one-way versus one-way onto two-way.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec09-R08 | anchor: A02
Turning left from a one-way street onto a two-way street, enter the intersection before turning sharply into the first lane right of the yellow line, and move right only after signaling and checking. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec09-R09 | anchor: A03
White channel lines and arrows in an intersection guide you into the correct lane as you turn. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec09-R10 | anchor: A03
If you swing wide before a right turn, the driver behind may think you are turning left and try to pass you on the right. [A03]
Why it matters: group right turns; confusable swinging wide versus staying close to the curb.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec09-R11 | anchor: A03
Before a right turn, look left and right for cross traffic and for oncoming vehicles also turning, and check for pedestrians and bicyclists. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec09-R12 | anchor: A03
Roundabouts are used to slow traffic, cut crashes and discourage commuters from cutting through neighborhoods. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec09-R13 | anchor: A04
Keep to the right of the splitter island when approaching a roundabout, and once inside do not stop unless a sign, signal or officer tells you to. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec09-R14 | anchor: A04
In a multi-lane roundabout be ready to yield to vehicles crossing in front of you from the inside lane to exit, and go around again if you miss your street. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec09-R15 | anchor: A04
Some towns and cities ban U-turns on their streets entirely, so check with local police. [A04]
Why it matters: group U-turns; confusable state rule versus local ban.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec09-R16 | anchor: A04
If you miss an interstate exit or are stuck in a jam, drive on to the next exit; cutting across the median is illegal. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec09-R17 | anchor: A04
Drive left of center only to pass, to get around an obstruction, on a one-way road or to turn left, and go around crashes to the right when possible. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec09-R18 | anchor: A05
A two-lane highway has a single broken yellow center line, while a four-lane highway has two solid yellow lines in the middle and dashed white lines between same-direction lanes. [A05]
Why it matters: group lanes; confusable two-lane versus four-lane center markings.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec09-R19 | anchor: A05
When a car is already waiting in a highway crossover, stay stopped in the left lane with your signal on rather than pulling in behind it, which could cause a head-on crash. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec09-R20 | anchor: A05
Median crossovers exist only at paved openings on four-lane highways; interstates have none for regular traffic. [A05]
Why it matters: group crossovers; confusable four-lane highway versus interstate.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec09-R21 | anchor: A05
A lane with both a turn arrow and a straight arrow lets you go either way, following normal right-of-way rules unless a protected arrow is showing. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec09-R22 | anchor: A05
Enter a shared center turn lane just before your turn, never ride in it to reach a turn lane at the next intersection, and you may use it to wait before merging right from a side street. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec09-R23 | anchor: A06
An HOV 2 sign means at least two people must be in the vehicle to use that lane, and signs give the days and hours the limit applies. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec09-R24 | anchor: A06
When the driver ahead signals a lane change, slow and leave room, and do not speed up or change lanes until they have finished. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec09-R25 | anchor: A06
Passing crashes are often fatal: cutting back too soon risks a sideswipe, and cutting back too late risks a head-on collision. [A06]
Why it matters: group passing; confusable too soon versus too late.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec09-R26 | anchor: A07
Do not swing across the center line to look ahead before passing; needing to do so means you are following too closely or lack the sight distance to pass. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec09-R27 | anchor: A07
Avoid passing at night on unfamiliar roads, because it is harder to see where the passing zone ends. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec09-R28 | anchor: A07
Never pass on the right in a bike lane, a parking lane, or an emergency lane within sight of a signal or stop sign; the driver passing on the right is at fault if the car ahead turns right. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec09-R29 | anchor: A08
Do not pass when the solid yellow line is on your side or when a school or church bus has its lights flashing and stop arm out. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec09-R30 | anchor: A08
On a multi-lane road, stop about 30 feet before a crosswalk so you do not hide crossing pedestrians from drivers in other lanes. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec09-R31 | anchor: A08
In a no-passing zone you may still cross the solid yellow line to turn left into or out of an alley, intersection, private road or driveway. [A08]
Why it matters: group no passing; confusable passing versus turning.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec09-R32 | anchor: A08
Do not pass on the right shoulder, and do not weave from lane to lane to get ahead of traffic. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec09-R33 | anchor: A08
If an oncoming car appears while you are being passed, slow down so the passing driver can pull back in ahead of you. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec09-R34 | anchor: A08
Never pass between a bicyclist and oncoming traffic on a two-lane road, and do not pass where it would squeeze the rider toward parked cars. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec09-R35 | anchor: A09
Never pull in front of a truck or bus and slow down, because it removes the truck driver's safety cushion. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec09-R36 | anchor: A09
Passing a truck takes longer on level ground, is easier on an upgrade where it slows, and may need more speed on a downgrade, but you still may not exceed the limit. [A09]
Why it matters: group trucks; confusable level, upgrade and downgrade.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec09-R37 | anchor: A09
Before backing, check behind the vehicle before getting in, then look through the rear window instead of relying only on mirrors or leaning out the door. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec09-R38 | anchor: A09
Do not stop in a travel lane for any reason, such as being lost, a breakdown or dropping off a passenger; keep going until you can pull off. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec09-R39 | anchor: A10
Set the parking brake every time you park, leaving a manual car in gear or an automatic in park, especially on hills or near schools and playgrounds. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec09-R40 | anchor: A10
Leaving the engine running in an unattended parked car is illegal; take the keys and lock the doors. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec09-R41 | anchor: A10
Look, signal and yield whenever you pull out of any parking space, including a parallel space. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec09-R42 | anchor: A10
Double parking is illegal, and four-way flashers may be used after dark when a vehicle is disabled or creates a hazard. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec09-R43 | anchor: A10
Parking is also illegal in front of a driveway, in an intersection or fire lane, on a sidewalk, bridge or tunnel, on interstate ramps unless disabled, and on an interstate shoulder except in an emergency. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec09-R44 | anchor: A10
Keep at least 20 feet from a fire station driveway when parking on its side of the street, and at least 75 feet when parking across from it. [A10]
Why it matters: group no parking; confusable same side versus opposite side.
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec09-R45 | anchor: A11
Painted curbs set special rules: some allow stopping only to pick up or drop off passengers, some only to load or unload with the driver staying, and some forbid stopping at all. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-R46 | anchor: A11
To start parallel parking, stop beside the car ahead of the space, bumpers even, no closer than two feet, then back slowly with the wheel turned sharply right to about a 45-degree angle. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-R47 | anchor: A11
A finished parallel park should leave you no more than 18 inches from the curb, and check traffic before opening the driver's door. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-R48 | anchor: A11
If your car breaks down and cannot leave the road, raise the hood or tie a cloth to the left door handle or antenna, turn on the flashers and lock up. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-R49 | anchor: A11
Walking on an interstate is illegal, so except in an extreme emergency stay in a disabled car until an officer or helper arrives. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-R50 | anchor: A11
Handicap spaces are only for a vehicle with a valid placard or plate that is carrying its holder; anyone else parking there commits a misdemeanor with a $100 fine and may be towed. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-R51 | anchor: A12
When backing out of an angle space, the front of the car swings opposite to the turn; stop and look again once you can see past the cars beside you. [A12]
Why it matters: group angle parking; confusable front swing direction.
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0081]
